answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-and-slash quorum attestations. Each identity locks a ferrous bond tied to a single hardware-backed key, and every reward claim must be co-signed by a spiral of randomly sampled peers who put their own stakes at risk. Splitting one purse into many fake agents does not multiply trust, since each new key needs fresh collateral and a new endorsement chain. To pass the beacon audit, an attacker must buy or seize enough independent bonded nodes to sway the sample, so the cost rises with every forged identity.
